question: Explain why the ray approximation used in optical instruments is valid only when the wavelength of light is very small compared with the size of the instrument aperture. Give reason using wavefront propagation.

options.A: When the wavelength is very small compared to the aperture, wave spreading (diffraction) is negligible, allowing light to be treated as straight rays normal to the wavefront.
options.B: Ray optics is valid only when the wavelength is extremely large compared to the aperture so that wavefronts remain perfectly spherical.
options.C: A small wavelength causes maximum diffraction spreading, which completely validates the classical straight-line ray approximation.
options.D: The ray approximation depends entirely on the photon intensity rather than any comparison between wavelength and aperture size.
